title: The unduloid Lagena shell is formed while hanging vertically in the sea

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The unduloid Lagena shell is formed while hanging vertically in the sea

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The flask-shaped (unduloid) shell of Lagena is formed while the organism hangs vertically, in a position of symmetry about its vertical axis, like a hanging drop; flattened or winged forms are those formed when this symmetry of position was absent and the shell lay horizontally.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: but we may be pretty sure that it is suspended vertically in the sea, that is to say in a position of symmetry as regards its vertical axis, about which the unduloid surface of revolution is symmetrically formed.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Foraminiferal shells and position of symmetry”. Scope: monothalamous calcareous foraminifera (Lagena) and, by extension, flask-shaped pteropod shells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-20: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.44

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Orientation, growth state, and shell symmetry give a direct prospective test. Existing occurrence and specimen images show final form but not the organism's posture when that form was produced, so the central temporal variable is missing.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure live Lagena orientation during shell deposition and test whether axisymmetric shells grow while vertical whereas flattened or winged shells grow while horizontal.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Live observations of shell deposition in these taxa are scarce.

Public shell images do not record orientation during calcification.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Shell archives are good enough to test whether flask-shaped Lagena are surfaces of revolution and winged forms are not. The claim itself is about orientation during formation, and that life-position variable is not in those collections. Shape is a usable proxy with a serious confound, so only part of the claim can be resolved now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit Lagena tests to a surface of revolution and compare that symmetry class with any records of orientation during calcification. Unduloids formed while the axis is vertical, and winged tests formed while it is horizontal, would support the claim; the reverse pairing would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
An unduloid of revolution is also the expected outcome of any axisymmetric growth rule, so shape alone does not identify a hanging-drop posture.

Public images record finished tests, not the posture of the living cell while the shell was secreted.
